newsitem.title: USA: FDA sets standards for wires for health devices.
newsitem.headline: FDA sets standards for wires for health devices.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration on Thursday set new safety standards for electrical wires that connect patients to medical devices.
The FDA said the rule applies to wires called cables and leads that are used with breathing, heart, and brain wave monitors.

It requires that the wires be "protected" which means they cannot be mistakenly plugged into electrical outlets and cause death or injury by burning or electrocution. Such accidents are rare but they have occurred.
The wires have an electrode at one end that attaches to the patient and the other end goes into a monitor or other medical device.

The new rules are in keeping with the international standards that have been developed for these products, the FDA said. Many manufacturers already voluntarily have protected wires. The new standards will be phased in over three years, with the riskiest products having to meet the standards in one year.
